description: C++ Operators, Type Casting, Strings and Conditions Practice

questions.questionText: Which operator is used for addition in C++?
questions.explanation: The + operator is used to add two values.

questions.questionText: What is the result of 10 / 3 when both operands are integers?
questions.explanation: Integer division discards the fractional part, so 10 / 3 gives 3.

questions.questionText: Which operator gives the remainder after integer division?
questions.explanation: The modulus (%) operator returns the remainder of integer division.

questions.questionText: What is the value of 17 % 5 in C++?
questions.explanation: 17 divided by 5 leaves a remainder of 2. Therefore, 17 % 5 is 2.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to check equality between two values?
questions.explanation: The == operator compares two values for equality.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used for assignment in C++?
questions.explanation: The = operator assigns a value to a variable.

questions.questionText: Which operator means 'not equal to' in C++?
questions.explanation: The != operator checks whether two values are different.

questions.questionText: Which logical operator represents AND in C++?
questions.explanation: The && operator returns true when both conditions are true.

questions.questionText: Which logical operator represents OR in C++?
questions.explanation: The || operator returns true when at least one condition is true.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used for logical NOT?
questions.explanation: The ! operator reverses a Boolean value.

questions.questionText: What is the output of int x = 5; cout << ++x;?
questions.explanation: The pre-increment operator increments x before its value is used, so 6 is printed.

questions.questionText: What is the output of int x = 5; cout << x++;?
questions.explanation: Post-increment uses the current value first and increments it afterward, so 5 is printed.

questions.questionText: Which operator is known as the conditional or ternary operator?
questions.explanation: The ?: operator is called the conditional or ternary operator.

questions.questionText: Which syntax correctly converts an integer to a double using C-style casting?
questions.explanation: The C-style cast syntax (double)x converts x to double.

questions.questionText: Which C++ casting operator is specifically used for basic compile-time type conversions?
questions.explanation: static_cast is commonly used for explicit compile-time type conversions.

questions.questionText: Which header file is required to use the std::string class?
questions.explanation: The std::string class is provided by the <string> header.

questions.questionText: Which declaration correctly creates a C++ string?
questions.explanation: With using namespace std;, string name = "Nityanand"; is a valid std::string declaration.

questions.questionText: Which function returns the number of characters in a std::string?
questions.explanation: Both length() and size() return the number of characters in a std::string.

questions.questionText: Which function is commonly used to read a complete line including spaces into a string?
questions.explanation: std::getline() reads an entire line, including spaces, from an input stream.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to make a decision using a condition?
questions.explanation: The if statement executes a block when its condition is true.

questions.questionText: Which statement is used when there are two alternative blocks based on a condition?
questions.explanation: The if-else statement provides two alternative execution paths.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int x = 10; if (x > 5) cout << "Yes"; else cout << "No";
questions.explanation: Since 10 is greater than 5, the if block executes and prints Yes.

questions.questionText: Which operator checks whether one value is greater than another?
questions.explanation: The > operator checks whether the left operand is greater than the right operand.

questions.questionText: What is the value of the expression (5 > 3) && (2 < 4)?
questions.explanation: Both conditions are true, so the logical AND expression evaluates to true.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int a = 10, b = 20; cout << (a > b ? a : b);
questions.explanation: The condition a > b is false, so the ternary operator returns b, which is 20.
